historical_record.description: The Victorian house here was built between 1891 and 1893 on a seven-lot property fronting Sunnyside Avenue.

The house was first listed as 230 and then as 236 Sunnyside Avenue. Its builder, a streetcar gripman, sold the property to William Augustus Merralls, the mining engineer and inventor who built the conservatory next door.

Merralls's second wife set out to make the house and grounds a sanitorium, which she named Sunnyside Laboratories: a convalescent area was begun in the attic and the shingled extension on the east side was added. The work was never finished.
